look_here_first: Inspect the END of one intact comb and look for a conspicuous bare, pointed branch-axis extension ('stinger') beyond the last spikelets. On fresh branches check for long spreading hairs and on basal blades for papillose-based hairs. Hairiness alone varies and does not trump terminal spikelet/rachis anatomy.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hagenbuch & Lemke's Texas Hill Country grass treatment documents native/herbarium records from Burnet, Comal, and Hays counties, among additional project-zone counties.

best_field_traits: papillose-based hairs especially near blade margins/base
branch axis extends beyond terminal spikelets as a naked point
spikelets often green to dark purple
rudimentary florets with conspicuous short awns
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Compared with Bouteloua pectinata, B. hirsuta is generally shorter and less robust, with fewer/shorter inflorescence branches and a longer flowering window. Compared with B. trifida, it has broader comb-like branches with many more tightly packed spikelets.
crew_field_steps: Find an intact one-sided flowering comb; don't just notice its purple or tan color.
Trace the branch to its naked projecting tip beyond the packed spikelets. The inspected close photo shows that needlelike extension clearly.
Examine the long spreading hairs on branch and basal blade margins; compare blue grama, which usually lacks the long bare terminal rachis.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Whole flowering plant with number of racemes on same culm and height context.
True branch-tip extreme macro showing spikelets stop BEFORE extended naked rachis.
Papillose-based basal leaf/blade hair macro and sheath/ligule.
Mature comb and spikelets against a millimeter ruler next to B. gracilis/B. pectinata.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Compared with blue grama, hairy grama has more conspicuously hairy reproductive parts and a naked projecting rachis tip; blue comb spikelets continue toward the tip. Taller B. pectinata often has longer, straighter and more numerous combs, but their features overlap enough to require mature units and provenance. Texas grama bears several very short highly awned/fuzzy branches rather than a few longer solid combs.

measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.look_here_first: Hairy grama: inspect the end of one intact comb for a bare rachis tip extending 5–10 mm past the final spikelets; check papillose-based hairs on glume midveins and basal blade margins. Do not diagnose solely by purple color or the word 'hairy'.

measurable_diagnostics.growth_form: Warm-season tufted perennial, sometimes short-stoloniferous; culms approximately 15–75 cm in Iowa State's grass treatment, commonly 20–50 cm in Texas field descriptions.
measurable_diagnostics.ligule_collar: Ligule a fringe of hairs approximately 0.2–0.5 mm (Iowa State); collar may be hairy, auricles not used as a species character. Photograph the actual blade/sheath junction and papillose-based marginal hairs with mm scale.
measurable_diagnostics.flowering_architecture: Usually 1–4 short one-sided combs; each often 1.5–3 cm long with approximately 20–50 closely packed spikelets. Bare terminal rachis projects about 5–10 mm beyond the final spikelets; measure from last spikelet, not from comb base.
measurable_diagnostics.spikelet_glumes: Spikelets approximately 5–6 mm; each with one fertile and one or two reduced sterile florets. Lower glume approximately 1.4–3.5 mm, upper approximately 3–6 mm, with papillose-based hairs particularly on upper-glume midvein.
measurable_diagnostics.lemmas_florets_awns: Fertile lemma approximately 2–4.5 mm, often pubescent and 1–3 short-awned (central awn approximately 0.2–2.5 mm). Reduced sterile lemma often bilobed and 3-awned, awns approximately 2–4(–6) mm. The naked rachis 'stinger' is NOT a lemma awn.

measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.local_lookalikes: Bouteloua gracilis (blue grama) usually has more spikelets per comb and little bare rachis extension beyond the last spikelet, and is less papillose-hairy; B. pectinata can have more numerous/longer combs but overlaps and may hybridize, requiring a complete specimen and current taxonomy; B. trifida has very short, more feathery branches rather than the solid comb of hairy grama.
last_mile_photo_arrow_gaps: Whole rooted perennial crown and complete flowering culm with comb count, plus matched blue grama at same scale.
Undamaged comb tip with a 1-mm ruler proving 5–10 mm bare terminal rachis; annotate the rachis, not a floret awn.
Upper glume papillose-based hairs at 10–20× with 1-mm bar and separately basal blade-margin hairs and true ligule.
One dissected 5–6 mm spikelet with lower/upper glumes, fertile lemma and reduced sterile lemma separately exposed; show which awns attach to which lemma.
Matched B. gracilis/B. pectinata flowering branches with individually verified image rights and identification.
